# `Q-11-4` — Invalid Lua filter return value

> A Lua filter function returned something that cannot be converted to
> AST elements.

## What this means

A filter function's return value tells Quarto what to put in the
document where the matched element was. Only four kinds of return
value have a meaning:

| Return value          | Effect                                        |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `nil` (or no `return`) | keep the element unchanged                   |
| an element            | replace the element with this one             |
| a list of elements     | replace the element with all of them          |
| a string              | in inline contexts only, becomes a `Str`      |

Anything else — a number, a boolean, a bare Lua table, a function —
has no AST equivalent, so Quarto stops and names the offending filter
function and the type it returned:

```
Q-11-4: filter function 'Str' returned an unsupported value: got number
```

## Why this happens

- **Returning the result of an expression by reflex.** `return #elem.content`
  or `return true` from a function whose purpose was really to inspect,
  not transform.
- **Returning a raw table** built by hand instead of a constructed
  element: `return { t = "Str", text = "hi" }` rather than
  `return pandoc.Str("hi")`.
- **Returning a number or string in a block context.** A string is
  accepted in inline positions only; a `Para` handler must return a
  block.
- **A stray `return` inside a conditional** that falls through to a
  value meant for something else.

## How to fix

Return `nil` when the element should be left alone — most filter
functions that only inspect should end without a `return` at all:

```lua
function Str(elem)
  if elem.text:match("TODO") then
    io.stderr:write("found a TODO\n")
  end
  -- no return: element is kept as-is
end
```

Return a constructed element when replacing:

```lua
function Str(elem)
  return pandoc.Str(elem.text:upper())
end
```

Return a list to replace one element with several, or with none:

```lua
function Para(elem)
  return {}          -- delete this paragraph
end
```

If you need a block-level result from a string, wrap it:
`return pandoc.Plain(pandoc.Str("text"))`.
